fullPassage: Punishing a child may not be effective due to what Álvaro Bilbao, a neuropsychologist, calls ‘trick-punishments.’ A trick-punishment is a scolding, a moment of anger or a punishment in the most classic sense of the word. Instead of discouraging the child from doing something, it encourages them to do it. For example, Hugh learns that when he hits his little brother, his mother scolds him. For a child who feels lonely, being scolded is much better than feeling invisible, so he will continue to hit his brother. In this case, his mother would be better adopting a different strategy. For instance, she could congratulate Hugh when he has not hit his brother for a certain length of time. The mother clearly cannot allow the child to hit his little brother, but instead of constantly pointing out the negatives, she can choose to reward the positives. In this way, any parent can avoid trick-punishments.

④ a longer scolding: 더 긴 꾸중 — 반대
det.tip: would be better adopting a different strategy = 다른 전략을 쓰는 편이 낫다

questions.passage: Punishing a child may not be effective due to what Álvaro Bilbao, a neuropsychologist, calls ‘trick-punishments.’ A trick-punishment is a scolding, a moment of anger or a punishment in the most classic sense of the word. Instead of discouraging the child from doing something, it encourages them to do it. For example, Hugh learns that when he hits his little brother, his mother scolds him. For a child who feels lonely, being scolded is much better than feeling invisible, so he will continue to hit his brother. In this case, his mother would be better adopting a different strategy. For instance, she could congratulate Hugh when he has not hit his brother for a certain length of time. The mother clearly cannot allow the child to hit his little brother, but instead of constantly pointing out the negatives, she can choose to __________. In this way, any parent can avoid trick-punishments.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 빈칸 = reward the positives(긍정적인 면을 보상하다)
det.analysis:
① repeat the scolding: 꾸중을 반복하다 — 글의 취지와 반대
② increase the anger: 화를 키우다 — 부적절
③ ignore the problem: 문제를 무시하다 — 부적절
④ reward the positives: 부정적인 면을 지적하는 대신 긍정적인 면을 보상하다 ←정답 (앞의 pointing out the negatives와 대조)
det.tip: instead of pointing out the negatives, reward the positives (부정 지적 ↔ 긍정 보상)
